findings.mechanism: The attributed trace begins with the command to retrieve the benefaction, then meets the repeated temporal units, the cradle and maturity markers, and the two recorded speech acts. The long catalogue therefore reads as ordered entries rather than a loose list of praises.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels why the command to remember matters: it reconstructs a sequence whose stages and final reception are all part of the recalled gift.
findings.containment: This remains a medium-confidence attributed organization of the supplied ayah. It does not claim an external chronology or replace the plain command and its remembered events.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus trace identifies the command, favor, life-stage, and speech contacts, but the source is legacy_unbound and its synthesis remains attributed.

findings.title: Exploratory prepared-substrate pattern
findings.claim: The cradle and the shaped clay can be read, exploratorily, as two prepared substrates enabled to perform an unexpected mature or living function.
findings.mechanism: The attributed preparation facets at the cradle and shaped form meet the focus occurrences for speech, clay, and flight. Their contact places infant speech and clay animation in one possible prepared-substrate pattern without equating the two scenes.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can notice preparation before function in both scenes, while keeping the cradle, the clay, the speech, and the bird distinct.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory attributed analogy. It does not make infant development identical with clay animation, does not activate unlisted facets, and does not displace either ordinary reading.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus trace supplies all cited coordinates and a stated containment, but the outlier is explicitly exploratory and the source identity is legacy_unbound.
